senses.domain: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior
senses.def: pertaining to purity of motives
struggle against opposition
senses.comment: It is also possible to interpret ἄθλησις in Hebrews 10:32 as meaning ‘challenge’ (see 74.13).

senses.def: a test of someone’s capability to resist or to respond to some difficulty
senses.comment: For another interpretation of ἄθλησις in Hebrews 10:32, see 50.3.

senses.def: pertaining to being without change or wavering in one’s faith
an aromatic resin of a lily-like plant, often used for embalming a corpse
senses.comment: As in the case of σμύρνα ‘myrrh’ (6.208), translators normally borrow a term for ‘aloes’ and then employ some kind of marginal note to indicate the nature of the substance.

senses.def: to cry or shout with unusually loud volume
to persuade, with the possible implication of resistance and/or for wrong motives or results
to oppose someone, involving not only a psychological attitude but also a corresponding behavior
senses.comment: In translating this phrase in Galatians 2:11 it may be appropriate in some languages to say ‘I spoke against him with other people present.’

senses.def: to resist by actively opposing pressure or power
senses.comment: In a number of languages one may appropriately translate ‘to resist’ in a number of contexts as ‘to fight back against’ or ‘to oppose in return.’ In some contexts, however, such as Acts 7:51, the meaning may perhaps be best expressed by a negation, for example, ‘you have never been willing to yield to the Holy Spirit.’

senses.def: to face straight ahead
glosses: to face into (for example, the wind)

senses.def: (derivative of ἀπιστέω[a] ‘to not believe,’ 31.39) pertaining to not being believable
(derivative of ἀπιστέω[b] ‘to not believe (in),’ 31.97) pertaining to not believing, with the implication of refusing to believe
one who does not believe the good news about Jesus Christ
glosses: one who is not a believer
senses.comment: It is clearly not enough in most languages to render ἄπιστος[b] in Mark 9:19 (see 31.98).

senses.domain: Groups and Classes of Persons and Members of Such Groups and Classes
senses.def: a person who does not belong to the group of believers in Christ
senses.comment: In 1 Corinthians 7:15 it may be necessary to indicate the so-called goal of belief or trust, for example, ‘if one who is not a believer in Christ’ or ‘if the one who is not a follower of Christ.’

senses.def: to sail away from a point

senses.subdomain: Acceptable To, To Be Pleased With
senses.def: pertaining to that which pleases someone
senses.comment: In some languages the equivalent of ‘this pleased the Jews’ is ‘this caused the Jews to be happy’ or even ‘this caused the Jews to say, That’s fine.’

senses.def: pertaining to being proper or right, with the implication of desirable
to live in a manner contrary to proper religious beliefs and practice
glosses: to live in an ungodly manner

senses.subdomain: A Point of Time with Reference to Units of Time: Daybreak, Midday, Midnight, Late
senses.def: the point of time when the day begins

senses.domain: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior
senses.def: to engage in behavior which is totally wrong and harmful
any of the smaller green plants (in Hellenistic Greek often used in contexts referring to plants as fodder for animals)
senses.comment: βοτάνη is more generic in meaning than χόρτος[a], 3.15.

senses.def: a garden at the foot of the Mount of Olives
to engage in physical exercise as a way of improving the body
a city in Lycaonia
to argue about differences of opinion
to speak in a somewhat formal setting and probably implying a more formal use of language
(derivative of διδάσκω ‘to teach,’ 33.224) one who provides instruction
to try to learn the genuineness of something by examination and testing, often through actual use
glosses: to try to determine the genuineness of

senses.subdomain: To Choose, To Select, To Prefer
senses.def: to regard something as being worthwhile or appropriate
senses.comment: For another interpretation of δοκιμάζω in Romans 1:28, see 30.114.

senses.subdomain: To Distinguish, To Evaluate, To Judge
senses.def: to regard something as genuine or worthy on the basis of testing
senses.comment: For another interpretation of δοκιμάζω in Romans 1:28, see 30.98.

senses.def: cardinal number, where there are seventy instances of a countable entity
to swim out of or away from a structure or area

senses.subdomain: Low Status or Rank [including persons of low status]
senses.def: to cause something to have less status or rank

senses.subdomain: Low Status or Rank [including persons of low status]
senses.def: to decrease in status or rank
senses.comment: Compare αὐξάνω[d] ‘to become more important’ 87.37.

senses.def: to cause the process of burning to begin
senses.comment: As already noted in the series of terms listed in 14.63, languages differ appreciably in terms employed for different phases and results of burning. For example, to set something on fire for the sake of providing warmth may be expressed by quite a different term from that which is used in speaking of the process of setting something on fire in order to destroy it.|ἐμπίπρημι refers specifically to the process of setting something on fire, but obviously the implication in Matthew 22:7 is that the city was burned down. A number of translations, therefore, follow the implied component of ἐμπίπρημι and translate ‘he burned down their city.’ In some languages it may seem strange to speak of ‘burning down a city.’ A more natural expression would be ‘to burn down all the buildings of the city.’

senses.def: cardinal number, where there are nine instances of a countable entity
senses.comment: In Luke 17:17 there is a significant ellipsis, and so in some languages one may wish to translate ‘where are the other nine persons?’ or ‘… nine men?’

senses.def: to engage in a careful search in order to acquire information, though primarily by inquiry
glosses: to make a diligent effort to learn

senses.def: to inquire intently, with the implication of careful examination
a marker of cause or reason, often with the implication of a relevant temporal element
to provide information about a person or an event concerning which the speaker has direct knowledge
senses.comment: In a number of languages it is necessary to indicate specifically what is the content of a witness, so that, for example, in Luke 21:13 it may be necessary to say ‘this is your chance to witness to the good news’ or ‘… to tell about the good news’ or ‘… to tell what you yourselves know about the good news.’

senses.def: to change from darkness to light in the early morning hours
senses.comment: In some languages dawning is divided into more than one aspect or period of time. The first may be only a glimmering of light in the east; the second period makes visibility quite easy; and the third period involves shafts of light or colored clouds visible in the sky immediately before sunrise. Usually an expression for one of these periods of time is more generalized in usage, and therefore it is probably satisfactory to adopt such an expression for any transition from darkness to light.

senses.def: pertaining to a state of readiness
pertaining to being easily understood

senses.subdomain: Instruments Used in Agriculture and Husbandry
senses.def: a bar or frame of wood by which two draft animals are joined at the head or neck in order to work together effectively in pulling a plow, harrow, or wagon
senses.comment: ζυγός[a] occurs in the NT only in figurative contexts. In a sense, this means that ζυγός is itself figurative in meaning, but the figure of speech is an extended figure in which case individual components are normally regarded as having a literal meaning.

senses.def: an instrument for weighing objects
senses.comment: A balance scale may be described in some languages as ‘a tool for weighing’ or ‘an instrument for knowing how much something weighs.’ Ancient balance scales often consisted of a rod held by a cord in the middle and with pans attached to both ends. Weights could be placed in one pan, while the item to be weighed would be placed in the other.

senses.def: to deprive a person of life, with the implication of this being the result of condemnation by legal or quasi-legal procedures
(a figurative extension of meaning of θανατόω[a] ‘to put to death,’ 20.65) to cease completely from activity, with the implication of extreme measures taken to guarantee such a cessation
senses.comment: It is possible that in rendering this expression in Romans 8:13 one may desire to retain the figure of speech and therefore translate ‘if by the Spirit you put to death the works of the body.’

senses.def: domesticated four-footed animals, primarily livestock
senses.comment: τὰ θρέμματα in John 4:12 would include cattle (bulls, cows, oxen), sheep, goats, donkeys, and possibly camels. It is difficult, however, to obtain in certain languages an expression which is sufficiently generic as to include all such domesticated animals. Sometimes, however, one can use a phrase such as ‘animals that people take care of’ or ‘animals that are herded’ or even ‘animals that are owned.’

senses.def: the role of being a priest
(an idiom, literally: to follow in the tracks) to behave in the same manner as someone else
(an idiom, literally: to walk in the tracks) to behave in the same manner as someone else
(an idiom, literally: to follow in the tracks) to behave in the same manner as someone else
the process of burning
senses.comment: In a number of languages important distinctions are made in the use of terms for burning. For example, the burning of a substance for light, as in the case of a lamp or candle, may be indicated by a term quite different from an expression indicating the destruction or burning up of something. Similarly, the burning of wood for cooking may require still another term. The extent or size of the fire involved may also require some distinctions in terms for burning.

senses.def: to cause the process of burning to begin
senses.comment: As already noted in the series of terms listed in 14.63, languages differ appreciably in terms employed for different phases and results of burning. For example, to set something on fire for the sake of providing warmth may be expressed by quite a different term from that which is used in speaking of the process of setting something on fire in order to destroy it.|In a number of languages one must not speak of ‘a lamp burning’ or ‘to burn a lamp,’ for this would imply burning up a lamp or destroying it. It may therefore be necessary to say ‘to cause the wick of a lamp to burn’ or ‘to light the wick of a lamp,’ and instead of saying ‘the lamp burns,’ one may say ‘the lamp gives light’ or ‘the lamp shows a flame.’

senses.def: to break or to shatter a rigid object
to cause something or someone to sink into deep water
to sink down into deep water
(a figurative extension of meaning of κατοικίζω ‘to cause to dwell,’ not occurring in the NT) to cause to be in a place defined psychologically or spiritually
to make a change of location in space (a highly generic meaning)
senses.comment: A strictly literal translation of κινέω in Acts 17:28 might imply merely moving from one place to another. The meaning, however, is generalized movement and activity; therefore, it may be possible to translate κινούμεθα as ‘we come and go’ or ‘we move about’ or even ‘we do what we do.’

senses.def: to cause something to be moved from a place
senses.comment: It is also possible to translate κινέω in Revelation 2:5 as ‘I will take away.’

senses.def: to set something in motion, with the nature of the movement dependent upon the object in question
senses.comment: In Mark 15:29 the shaking of the head signifies derision and scorn, but in some languages this meaning is expressed by quite different gestures, for example, pointing with the finger, throwing back the head, or shrugging the shoulders. In fact, in some languages shaking the head from side to side means assent, while nodding shows opposition.

senses.def: to cause people to riot against

senses.subdomain: Agent in a Causative Role Marked by Verbs
senses.def: a marker of a causative relation, with the implication of significant activity
to cause something to be reduced in number or extent
senses.comment: There may be difficulties involved in a strictly literal rendering of ‘those days will be shortened,’ for it might appear that each day would become shorter rather than that the number of days would be decreased. Therefore, one must render this expression in Matthew 24:22 in a number of languages as ‘those days will be fewer.’

senses.def: act of deciding a question of legal right or wrong, and thus determining the innocence or guilt of the accused and assigning appropriate punishment or retribution
senses.comment: The process of legal judging is often expressed idiomatically. In Africa, one of the standard phrases for judging is ‘to cut a palaver,’ but other expressions in other languages may be ‘to find guilt,’ ‘to point the finger at wrong,’ or ‘to untangle strife.’

senses.def: (derivative of κρίνω[e] ‘to judge legal cases,’ 56.20) the authority or right to judge guilt or innocence
a court of justice for determining guilt or innocence
senses.comment: For languages which do not have technical terms for a court, it is usually possible to use some such phrase as ‘to be brought before a judge’ or ‘to have judges decide one’s case.’

senses.def: the legal decision rendered by a judge, whether for or against the accused
act of judging a person to be guilty and liable to punishment
the administration of justice
senses.comment: It may be difficult to speak of ‘justice triumphing,’ and so in some languages it may be necessary to translate ‘so that all accusations are judged justly’ or ‘so that everyone receives what he should’ or ‘until all judgments are just.’

senses.subdomain: To Distinguish, To Evaluate, To Judge
senses.def: (derivative of κρίνω[c] ‘to judge,’ 30.108) the content of the process of judging
senses.comment: It may also be possible to translate ἀλλὰ τὴν δικαίαν κρίσιν κρίνετε (John 7:24) as ‘judge in a righteous manner’ or ‘judge according to true standards.’

senses.subdomain: To Distinguish, To Evaluate, To Judge
senses.def: the basis for rendering a judgment
senses.comment: It is also possible to render κρίσις in John 3:19 as ‘how judgment works’ or ‘the reason for God judging.’

senses.def: punishment, with the implication of having been judged guilty
senses.comment: It is also possible, of course, to interpret κρίσις in Matthew 23:33 as meaning ‘condemnation’ (see 56.30), but as such, punishment is certainly implied.

senses.def: (an idiom, literally: to fall under judgment) to be condemned for acting contrary to laws and regulations
senses.comment: In the context of James 5:12 the condemnation refers to God’s judgment.

senses.def: (derivative of λαλέω ‘to speak,’ 33.70) that which has been spoken or uttered
a particular manner of speech

senses.subdomain: Cloth, Leather, and Objects Made of Such Materials
senses.def: linen cloth, normally in the form of a garment
senses.comment: Linen garments may be described as ‘clothing made out of linen cloth.’ What is important in Revelation 15:6 is the quality of the garments, not so much the fact that they were made of linen

senses.subdomain: Cloth, Leather, and Objects Made of Such Materials
senses.def: a linen cord in a lamp that draws up the oil
senses.comment: A wick may often be referred to as ‘a small strip of cloth.’

senses.def: the father of Eli in the genealogy of Jesus
the father of Jorim in the genealogy of Jesus
the upper range of a scale of extent, with the possible implication of importance in relevant contexts
senses.comment: In a number of languages the expression of intense degree associated with some activity or state is expressed by means of a verb, not an adverb, so that one may render Philippians 4:10 literally as ‘I am-intense joyous in the Lord,’ in which the form ‘am-intense’ is an attempt to represent a verb expression in such a language.

senses.def: to change the essential form or nature of something
senses.comment: In a number of languages the equivalent of μεταμορφόομαι in Romans 12:2 may be ‘become completely different’ or ‘become different from what you are.’

senses.subdomain: Appearance as an Outward Manifestation of Form
senses.def: to take on a different physical form or appearance
senses.comment: In some instances it may be more appropriate to render this expression in Mark 9:2 as ‘as they watched, he appeared different.’

senses.def: the chief city on the island of Lesbos in the Aegean Sea
an alternative form of Ναζαρηνός, 93.537 (Matthew 2:23)
(derivative of νόμος[a] ‘law, rule,’ 33.333) pertaining to law
senses.comment: It is also possible to understand νομικός in Titus 3:9 as specifically the Jewish Law (see νόμος[b], 33.55).

senses.def: one who is an expert in interpreting religious law (with a probable exception of Titus 3:13 (see 56.37), always in reference to the Jewish Law)
a specialist in civil law
senses.comment: It is possible that νομικός in Titus 3:13 may have designated an expert in interpreting religious law (see 33.338) rather than a general legal practitioner.

senses.def: to possess information about
to have the knowledge as to how to perform a particular activity or to accomplish some goal
to comprehend the meaning of something, with focus upon the resulting knowledge
to be able to recall from memory

senses.subdomain: Honor or Respect in Relation to Status
senses.def: to acknowledge the high status of a person or event
pertaining to being similar to something else in some respect
any kind of bird, wild or domestic
senses.comment: All languages have at least some terms for birds, but there may be no generic term which identifies birds while excluding all other creatures which fly. For example, in some languages a term which includes all kinds of birds also includes flying insects and bats. However, since in most instances such a term has birds as its primary reference, it can usually be employed in contexts in which birds are more or less readily identified by other expressions in the passage. In other languages generic terms for birds may identify only certain classes of birds, for example, birds of prey, water birds, and birds of the forest.|In this only NT occurrence (with parallel), ὄρνις probably designates a hen.

senses.subdomain: A Point of Time with Reference to Units of Time: Daybreak, Midday, Midnight, Late
senses.def: pertaining to a point near the end of a day (normally after sunset but before night)

senses.subdomain: Definite Units of Time: Year, Month, Week, Day, Hour
senses.def: the period after sunset and before darkness (compare 67.191)
that which has been entrusted to the care of someone
glosses: what is someone’s responsibility to care for

senses.subdomain: To Think About, with the Implied Purpose of Responding Appropriately
senses.def: act of intentionally not regarding or being concerned about certain objects or events
to cause someone to depart for a particular purpose
to cause someone to carry something to some destination
to send a message, presumably by someone
to cause someone to experience an event or state from outside the area of normal influences
(an idiom, literally: to send a sickle) to begin to harvest a crop by cutting ripe grain with a sickle
senses.comment: In Revelation 14:15 and Revelation 14:18 this idiom occurs in a figurative context, and therefore it may be necessary in some languages to speak of ‘harvesting’ rather than using a phrase which mentions the literal use of a sickle.

senses.def: pertaining to causing a decided or distinct advantage
pertaining to that which is exceptional in the sense of being more than what is expected
pertaining to a quantity so abundant as to be considerably more than what one would expect or anticipate
senses.comment: For another interpretation of περισσός in 2 Corinthians 9:1, see 71.40.

senses.def: pertaining to being unnecessary in view of being superfluous
senses.comment: For another interpretation of περισσός in 2 Corinthians 9:1, see 59.51.

senses.def: a degree which is considerably in excess of some point on an implied or explicit scale of extent
(an idiom, literally: from excess) an extremely high point on a scale of extent and implying excess
senses.comment: In Mark 6:51 both λίαν (78.1) and ἐκ περισσοῦ are expressions of degree and they reinforce one another.

senses.def: anything which is intertwined or interlaced, either woven or braided
pertaining to great affection and compassion

senses.subdomain: A Point of Time with Reference to Other Points of Time: Before, Long Ago, Now, At the Same Time, When, About, After
senses.def: a point of time prior to another point of time

senses.subdomain: Units of Time with Reference to Other Units or Points of Time: Yesterday, Today, Next Day
senses.def: the day immediately before the Sabbath
to carry or bring something into the presence of someone, usually implying a transfer of something to that person
to bring or lead into the presence of someone
glosses: to bring into the presence of

senses.def: to present something to someone, often involving actual physical transport of the object in question
to behave or act in a particular way with respect to someone
doors or gates used to close off entranceways
senses.comment: πύλη[a] and πυλών[a] may refer to house doors and gates or to large doors and gates such as were used in a palace, temple, or in a city wall.|Note, however, that in Acts 14:13 the reference may not be specifically to the gates as objects, but to the entranceway into the city.

senses.def: the area associated with the entrance into a house or building
senses.comment: The phrase τὰ πρὸς τὴν θύραν (see 7.39) is essentially equivalent to πυλών[b]: συνήχθησαν πολλοὶ ὥστε μηκέτι χωρεῖν μηδὲ τὰ πρὸς τὴν θύραν ‘so many people came together that there was no room left, not even out in the entrance’ Mark 2:2.

senses.def: a city thoroughfare which is relatively narrow
a reflexive reference to a receptor noted in the immediate context
senses.comment: For the plural, see 92.25.

senses.def: a collective for any kind of artifact which may be referred to by σκεῦος[a] ‘object, thing’ (6.1)
senses.comment: Wherever possible, it is useful to employ a rather specific term if this is well known in a receptor language. For example, instead of ‘things of a ship’ one may use ‘ship’s gear’ or ‘ship’s rigging.’

senses.def: to experience great affection and compassion for someone
a large organized group of soldiers
to tell someone what he or she should plan to do

senses.subdomain: To Intend, To Purpose, To Plan
senses.def: to engage in joint planning so as to devise a course of common action, often one with a harmful or evil purpose
that which ties something together
senses.comment: The context of Colossians 2:19 is, however, highly figurative.

senses.def: that which combines or brings objects and/or events together
two shallow and treacherous Mediterranean gulfs along the north African coastline
to cause something to become low in height
senses.comment: For another (probably preferred) interpretation of Luke 3:5, see 79.87.

senses.def: to cause something to become level
senses.comment: One might argue that ταπεινόω in Luke 3:5 is to be understood as ‘to be brought low,’ but in contrast with πληρωθήσεται, which refers to filling up valleys, ταπεινωθήσεται should perhaps be understood as referring to ‘leveling off’ mountains and hills. For this other interpretation of ταπεινόω in Luke 3:5, see 81.7.

senses.subdomain: Low Status or Rank [including persons of low status]
senses.def: to cause someone to be in a low status

senses.domain: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior
senses.def: (derivative of ταπεινός[b] ‘humble,’ 88.52) to cause someone to be or to become humble
senses.comment: A strictly literal rendering of ‘he who humbles himself’ could be misunderstood as ‘one who despises himself’ or ‘one who has no regard for himself.’ In the context of Matthew 18:4 it is often important to use an idiomatic expression which will adequately convey the meaning, for example, ‘one who causes his heart to bow down’ or even ‘one who makes his heart small.’

senses.def: to cause someone to become disgraced and humiliated, with the implication of embarrassment and shame

senses.subdomain: Low Status or Rank [including persons of low status]
senses.def: to live in circumstances regarded as characteristic of low status
glosses: to live like those of low status
senses.comment: In a number of languages ταπεινόομαι in Philippians 4:12 may be rendered as ‘to live like poor people.’

senses.def: to continue to hold in custody
senses.comment: The act of holding someone in custody or guarding an individual may be expressed as ‘standing guard to see that someone will not escape’ or ‘watching carefully so that one cannot run off’ or ‘tying someone up so that he cannot leave.’

senses.def: a place of detention
senses.comment: Practically all languages have terms for a jail or a prison, though in some instances a descriptive phrase is employed, ‘a place where people are tied up’ or ‘a place to be chained.’ In some instances, highly idiomatic expressions are used, ‘a place for eating iron’ or ‘a room with rats.’

senses.def: to continue to obey orders or commandments
the manner in which something is done
manner of life, often with focus upon customary acts
senses.comment: One may also render this expression in Hebrews 13:5 as ‘you should not be like people who always love money.’

senses.def: to be in a state, normally with the implication of a particular set of circumstances
to be identical with
to exist, particularly in relation to ownership
to belong to someone
(neuter plural participle of ὑπάρχω[d] ‘to belong to,’ 57.2) that which constitutes someone’s possession
a gentle blowing of the wind
senses.comment: In some instances a gentle wind may be described as ‘the air was just moving’ or ‘the air could just barely be felt’ or ‘the wind was just touching the skin.’

senses.def: pertaining to that which is bound to disintegrate and die

senses.subdomain: Instruments Used in Punishment and Execution
senses.def: an instrument consisting of either a single or multiple strips of leather with or without weighted tips on the ends; used to strike animals to make them move (faster), or as punishment on humans
senses.comment: The weighted tips of a φραγέλλιον would normally have been made of metal so as to increase the force of the blow and to inflict more severe punishment.

senses.def: a meaningful mark, whether engraved, imprinted, or branded
senses.comment: A strictly literal translation of ‘the mark of the beast’ might imply ‘a picture of the beast’ or ‘a mark made by the beast.’ A more satisfactory indication of the relationship between ‘mark’ and ‘beast’ would be ‘a mark showing one’s relationship to the beast’ or ‘a mark of loyalty to the beast’ or ‘a mark of the party of the beast.’

senses.def: an object (not necessarily three-dimensional) which has been formed to resemble a person, god, animal, etc.
senses.comment: In certain contexts the referents of εἰκών[a], τύπος[b], and χάραγμα[b] may have special religious significance in that they may refer to idols, but the focal component for the translator is that of a likeness or resemblance. In contexts such as Matthew 22:20 an equivalent translation may be simply ‘a picture,’ but in Romans 1:23 and Acts 7:43 one may use the same expression as is employed to render εἴδωλον[a] ‘idol’ (6.97).

senses.def: (literally: one who has been anointed) in the NT, titles for Jesus as the Messiah, but in many contexts, and especially without an article, Χριστός becomes a part of the name of Jesus; see 93.387)
senses.comment: In a number of languages Χριστός (or Μεσσίας) as a reference to the Messiah occurs in a transliterated form based either on Χριστός in Greek or on Messiah in Hebrew. However, in some languages an attempt is made to represent the significance of the terms Χριστός and Μεσσίας by translating ‘God’s appointed one’ or ‘God’s specially chosen one’ or ‘the expected one,’ in the sense of one to whom everyone was looking for help and deliverance.

senses.def: (the Greek translation of the Hebrew and Aramaic word ‘Messiah’) a proper name for Jesus; see also 53.82
a relatively weak marker of a relationship between events or states
a marker of discourse content, whether direct or indirect
senses.comment: The marking of direct and indirect discourse varies greatly from language to language. In some instances there is no marker at all; in other cases one marker precedes and another follows. In still other instances a repetition of an expression of speaking occurs at the end of a quotation, whether direct or indirect. In a number of languages written usage differs appreciably from spoken usage, because intonation so often marks introduced discourse in the spoken form of a language.

senses.def: a marker of an event indicating how something took place

senses.subdomain: A Point of Time with Reference to Other Points of Time: Before, Long Ago, Now, At the Same Time, When, About, After
senses.def: a point of time which is prior to another point of time, with the possible implication in some contexts of reason or cause

senses.subdomain: Duration of Time with Reference to Some Unit of Time: During, In, While, Throughout
senses.def: an extent of time of the same length as another extent or unit of time
a marker of cause or reason, implying the special nature of the circumstances
a marker of purpose, with the implication that what has preceded serves as a means
a marker of result, often in contexts implying an intended or indirect purpose
a degree which approximates a point on a scale of extent, either above or below
a relatively high point on a scale involving exclamation
senses.comment: In a number of languages an expression of high degree in an exclamation can only be reproduced as an expression of intensive degree in a non-exclamatory form. For example, the statement in Matthew 6:23 ‘how great must the darkness be!’ must be rendered in a number of languages as ‘the darkness is very, very intense’ or ‘it is very, very dark there.’

senses.def: (an idiom, literally: as to speak a word) an expression used to introduce an alternative form of expression as an interpretation of what has been said

senses.subdomain: A Point of Time with Reference to Other Points of Time: Before, Long Ago, Now, At the Same Time, When, About, After
senses.def: a point of time subsequent to another point of time, with an interval as brief as possible
senses.comment: In some languages the equivalent of ‘as soon as possible’ would involve a verb meaning ‘to hurry’ or ‘to do something quickly.’ Accordingly, Acts 17:15 may be rendered as ‘with instructions from him that Silas and Timothy hurry to join him.’
